description: What a friendly local can say about the place and the trouble. place_specific is keyed by location id (four lines each); place_generic, rumours and world are said freely; hints are the one useful, mechanically neutral pointer an NPC shares only once trusted. secret_keywords lists, per secret id in secrets.json, phrases no dossier may say in a public line. Every text is one speakable sentence. Original prose.

entries.text: The tide tables on the quay wall are chalked fresh each dawn by the same old woman.
Boats tied up after the evening bell lose their berth to whoever wants it.
The gulls here steal hats far more often than fish, and nobody has ever caught one at it.
The harbor-master's lamp burns until the last boat is in, and goes out the moment it is.
The charcoal burners hang a lantern at each crossing so that no one walks off the trail by night.
Pilgrims leave a pebble at the old cairn to ask for a safe road home.
The pines creak loudest before the weather turns, and the locals call it the trail talking.
Resin from these pines burns blue, and the lodge sells it by the cup.
The wind on the pass blows downhill in the morning and uphill by evening, so plan your climb by it.
Muleteers sing as they cross so the ones ahead will hear them in the cloud.
Three families have taken turns lighting the signal fires on the ridge for a hundred years.
Snow comes early on the north side of the pass, and it is always a surprise to somebody.
The stalls light their lanterns in order of age, oldest first.
The tea house takes every coin in the same cracked bowl and has never lost one.
Stall holders swap corners each festival so that nobody keeps the best spot for long.
The puppet show on Tin Street has run the same story for forty years, with a different ending every night.
The rooks at the gate roost on the same stones every night and bicker about it.
The caretaker rings the quiet bells softly so as not to wake anyone, and the sound carries all the same.
Mourners leave small lanterns by the gate, and the rooks have never once touched them.
The vestry door sticks in damp weather, and everyone has learned to lift and push.
The boardwalk planks are tarred each spring by whichever families live nearest.
The herons on the posts are said to count the boats, and the fen-folk nod to them as they pass.
The reeds hum a low note whenever the wind changes.
The eel-catchers sing to their traps, and they swear it helps.
The farm's well has never run dry, which the neighbours consider almost rude.
The owl in the hayloft has outlived three farm dogs.
Cider pressing is a village event, and everyone brings their own cup.
The mill wheel creaks in a pattern the children like to drum along to.
The great orrery is wound each dawn by the youngest scribe, as a rite of passage.
Silence is kept so strictly here that the library cats are the loudest residents.
The maps in the map room are copied and never lent.
The binding workshop smells of glue and cedar, and the apprentices fight over its warm corner.
Ask anyone around {location} about {destination} and they will tell you to go early and bring something for the host.
{location|cap} is quiet before noon and crowded after, and nobody can explain why.
Folk around {location} say good news travels slowly and bad news arrives before breakfast.
You can tell the hour around {location} by which neighbours are arguing.
{destination|cap} has been there longer than anyone's grandmother can remember, and she can remember quite a lot.
Strangers are welcome around {location}, so long as they say good evening.
Nobody around {location} will lend you an umbrella, but everyone will tell you it is going to rain.
The oldest saying around {location} is that every road ends at somebody's supper.
{destination|cap} keeps odd hours, so knock twice, wait, and do not take it personally.
People who leave {location} always come back, and they never admit they missed it.
The walk to {destination} is shorter than it looks and longer than it feels.
If you want to know the people around {location}, watch who holds the door.
People say {antagonist} has been seen near {location} after dark, asking quiet questions.
They say {antagonist} always works alone and always runs when outnumbered.
Folk around {location} have started locking their doors early since {antagonist_the} turned up.
A shopkeeper swears {antagonist_the} was in town three nights running.
The dogs bark all night whenever {antagonist_the} is near.
The old graves have been quieter than usual since {antagonist_the} walked, which people find worse.
Somebody paid a boy to follow {antagonist}, and the boy came back with nothing but mud.
Small things go missing wherever {antagonist} is about, spoons mostly.
Somebody chalked a child's drawing of {antagonist_the} on the wall by the well.
Most of what is said about {antagonist_the} is probably exaggerated, but not all of it.
{antagonist} was seen buying bread yesterday, which surprised everyone.
A song has started up about {antagonist_the}, and the verses get worse every time it is sung.
Word is {antagonist_the} is watching the road toward {destination}, waiting for anyone who carries {stake}.
Somebody has been asking after {stake} at every inn between {location} and {destination}.
The lamps along the road to {destination} have been put out by someone who does not want travelers seen.
Travelers who come through {location} lately will not say what they saw, only that they did not stay.
Whatever {antagonist_the} is, it has not been seen on the road toward {destination} in full daylight.
Two riders came through {location} before dawn, looking over their shoulders, and neither stopped to eat.
There is a price on {stake}, and not everyone who knows it is honest.
{destination|cap} keeps its doors barred after dark these nights, and opens them only for a name it knows.
If you lose sight of {antagonist_the}, check the narrow places around {location}, because that is where this sort of trouble goes to ground.
{antagonist} is more frightened than angry, so speak calmly and you will see it in the eyes before anything else.
The road toward {destination} is quietest an hour before dawn, and if trouble comes it will come when the light is worst.
Whoever you meet on the way, ask after {destination} by name first, because doors there open for a friendly mention.
{antagonist} flinches at a kind word, and I have never understood why.
Beasts like {antagonist_the} follow the smell of food, so keep whatever you carry well wrapped.
The dead do not follow roads, only memories, so keep to the lit path.
Listen for the noise around {location} to fall silent, because that is when trouble has arrived.
Whoever hired {antagonist_the}, if anyone did, was not paying much, since a full purse would have sent more than one.
Keep your voices low near {destination}, because the walls there carry sound into the next room.
If you want {antagonist} to listen, offer a seat and not a threat, because it works more often than you would think.
Watch the hands of anyone who greets you too warmly on the way, because the kindest faces are not always the kindest people.
{faction|cap} keeps a quiet watch on every road into {location}.
Anyone who asks {faction} politely for help gets it, and anyone who demands gets a long form to fill in.
People joke about {faction}, but nobody joked at their last meeting.
{faction|cap} has been recruiting lately, and the old hands do not like the new faces.
Folk say a figure called {villain} is behind a good deal of this, though nobody can say how they know.
Letters mentioning {villain} have been turning up where they should not, and nobody admits to writing them.
Whenever {villain} is mentioned, someone at the back of the room changes the subject.
Older folk will tell you to be careful what you say about {villain}, and will not tell you why.
I need {stake} carried to {destination}, and there is no one else I can ask.
Once {stake} is inside {destination}, I will sleep again; until then I do not.
The way to {destination} runs through {location}, and I would not linger there.
Keep {stake} out of sight on the road, because I have told no one it is moving.
I have been waiting at {destination} for {stake}, and I will not rest until it is inside.
{stake|cap} is safe behind the doors of {destination}, and not a moment before.
Nothing crosses from {location} to {destination} without somebody noticing, so move quietly.
I will have the door of {destination} open for you at any hour, so do not wait for daylight.
Hand over {stake} and this ends here.
Nothing passes {location} toward {destination} while I stand here.
I would not ask this of you if there were anyone else I could trust with it.
Every hour it stays unfinished weighs on me, so please do not dawdle.
I have kept everything ready on my side, and I will not be caught unprepared.
I have been watching the road for days, and I trust very few of the faces on it.
You will not get past me tonight, so spare yourselves the effort.
